title: Deeply Caramelised French Onion Dip with Chives and Crisps
summary: Onions are softened in butter and oil, then cooked low with splashes of water until deep brown, finished with cider vinegar and folded into soured cream and mayonnaise.
equipment: large (30 cm) frying pan with a lid

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.text: Melt the butter with the oil in the pan over medium-high heat. Add the onions, salt, pepper and cayenne, cover and cook 5 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise
steps.text: Uncover, lower the heat to medium-low and cook 35-45 minutes, stirring often. Each time a brown crust forms, add 2 tbsp water and scrape it up. Stop when the onions are deep mahogany.

steps.title: Finish the onions
steps.text: Stir in the vinegar for 1 minute, tip into the bowl and cool completely, about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Mix and chill
steps.text: Stir in the soured cream, mayonnaise, onion powder and garlic powder. Cover and chill at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Stir, taste, spoon into a bowl and scatter with chives. Serve cold with crisps.

tips: Don't rush the onions: the slow, deep browning is all the flavour.
Deglazing with water lifts the browned bits back into the onions.
The dip tastes even better the next day.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 4 days. Do not leave out for more than 2 hours. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
